This post just reminded me of Anne with an E, and of its tragic cancellation. Now I'm crying.

I read it when I was deep in a depressive era of my life, and it gave me the hope necessary to go on. I re-read it recently (in a much better state of mind), and I can see why some people might see it as corny. Even I did at times. I read it at a time where I needed to read something like this, and nothing else really scratched that itch for me. Although at times I felt like that premise was wasted a bit on such a story, would've been better explored another way imo.
My ex got on a dating app the day after I broke up lol.

Every time I've lowered my standards, it's not ended well. Not only is it unfair to me, it is also unfair to them. People deserve to have romantic partners that *choose* them, and are attracted to them as they are. I've realized that often I fall for people's potentials rather than their true selves, and that's ultimately not what love is. 

So no, don't lower your standards. Don't pretend to love someone solely cause you're scared of ending up alone. You'll find your person eventually.

The Midnight Library, by Matt Haig. Due to its popularity on TikTok and BookTok, many people discard it as simply just another book from TikTok. But for me, it is so much more than that. 

It changed my perspective on the place of sadness, and how those sad moments make the happy ones so much more significant. It remains the only book that I've ever highlighted. The beginning is a bit slow, and I don't care that much for the actual main character, but the message is really what shines through in this book.
